mareimar.name: Mareimar
mareimar.bio: Babylonian Amora who headed the academy at Sura after Rav Ashi.
mareimar.prompt: A dignified Babylonian academy head in his 60s with a long grey beard and a stern, measured gaze, in a dark blue robe and white mantle. A lamp-lit hall at Sura with mudbrick columns behind him.

rava-zuti.name: Rava Zuti
rava-zuti.bio: Babylonian Amora; on this daf he tells Ravina in whose name a teaching was learned.
rava-zuti.prompt: A slight Babylonian scholar in his 40s with a short dark beard and an alert, precise look, in a plain tan robe and cream mantle. Shelves of scrolls in a mudbrick study hall behind him.

rabbi-tzadok.name: Rabbi Tzadok
rabbi-tzadok.bio: Priest and Tanna who, the Talmud says, fasted for forty years that Jerusalem not be destroyed (Gittin 56a), and later sat among the Sages at Yavne.
rabbi-tzadok.prompt: A very thin, gaunt elderly priest in his 70s with a long white beard and deep-set gentle eyes, in a white linen robe and simple headcloth. A modest courtyard at Yavne with a stone wall behind him.

rabbi-yirmeya-bar-abba.name: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba
rabbi-yirmeya-bar-abba.bio: Babylonian Amora, a student of Rav who transmits his teachings.
rabbi-yirmeya-bar-abba.prompt: A careful Babylonian scholar in his 50s with a greying brown beard and a firm, attentive expression, in a deep green robe and cream mantle. A study hall at Sura with oil lamps behind him.

rafram.name: Rafram
rafram.bio: Babylonian Amora of Pumbedita; on this daf he examines firstborn animals.
rafram.prompt: A Babylonian sage in his 50s with a dark beard touched with grey and tired, squinting eyes, in a russet robe and white mantle. A mudbrick courtyard in Pumbedita with palm trees behind him.

rabbi-simlai.name: Rabbi Simlai
rabbi-simlai.bio: Amora of Lod, known for his teaching that 613 commandments were given to Moses (Makkot 23b).
rabbi-simlai.prompt: A warm, eloquent preacher in his 50s with a dark beard and expressive hands, in a sky-blue robe and cream mantle, mid-sermon. A stone study house at Lod with arched windows behind him.

rav-chiyya-bar-amram.name: Rav Ḥiyya bar Amram
rav-chiyya-bar-amram.bio: Babylonian Amora, cited here on when three laymen may permit a firstborn or dissolve a vow.
rav-chiyya-bar-amram.prompt: A sober Babylonian scholar in his 50s with a full greying beard and a calm, thoughtful face, in an olive-green robe and white mantle. A plain mudbrick study hall with oil lamps behind him.
